utility.value: Xcel Energy or Grand Valley Power, check your electric bill
utility.notes: Xcel Energy's list of Colorado communities served, dated 10/2015, shows Clifton with code GE, which means gas and electricity. The list is by community name, not by address. Mesa County's Power Districts map layer shows service areas for Grand Valley Power and Xcel Energy across the County. Its data is from November 2021, and it does not name Clifton. No official source names the utility for each Clifton address, so check the utility named on your electric bill before you apply for interconnection.

generation_supplier.notes: The supplier depends on which utility serves your address, Xcel Energy or Grand Valley Power, as named on your electric bill.

city.notes: Mesa County's residential permit clearance checklist lists Clifton Sanitation, at 3217 D Road, for sanitary sewer clearance.

county.notes: Mesa County's pages do not say which county Clifton is in.

permit_authority.value: Mesa County Building Department (for addresses in unincorporated Mesa County)
permit_authority.notes: Mesa County's Building Department says it performs inspections and supplies permits for building projects in the County and in the towns of De Beque, Collbran, Palisade, and the City of Grand Junction. It provides inspections for building permits for each of those jurisdictions and for unincorporated Mesa County. The County's Building Department pages do not say whether a Clifton address is in unincorporated Mesa County, so confirm with the Building Department which jurisdiction your address is in before you apply. The County's pages describe no expedited or same-day permit path for solar.

permit_url.notes: Use the Mesa County Customer Portal to submit a new permit and to view your current permits. The County's portal guide (revised 12-13-2021) says to click the green Permitting button to begin, and you can attach supporting documents with the Add Attachment button. For portal help, contact Mesa County Community Development at 970-244-1636 or MCComDev@mesacounty.us.

interconnection_url.notes: For Xcel Energy customers only. Xcel says that in most cases the developer or installer submits the interconnection application on your behalf, or you can manage your own, and the name on the application must match the name on the Xcel Energy account. Xcel highly recommends that construction of your system should not commence until your application receives full approval from the Xcel Energy engineering team and all final agreements are fully signed. Xcel says the interconnection work ends with a permission to operate letter from Xcel to the generator owner. If Grand Valley Power is your utility, ask Grand Valley Power about its interconnection process.

value.name: Renewable Battery Connect
value.description: Xcel says that when you add an eligible solar charged battery and participate, you let Xcel automatically manage your battery during periods of peak demand on the grid. Upfront incentive, General: $250 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to $5,000 per application). Income Qualified: $1,000 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). Disproportionately Impacted Community: $500 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). There is also a $100 annual participation incentive for all customer types for participating in control events (for 5-years).
value.eligibility: Xcel says eligible solar battery equipment includes all Tesla Powerwall models or all current Enphase models. Check that Xcel Energy is your utility first.

battery_programs.notes: Amounts are from Xcel's Renewable Battery Connect page, which shows 2026 budget figures dated 11/02/2026.

value: Submit the permit application on the Mesa County Customer Portal: click the green Permitting button and attach your documents.
For a residential ground mount system, get a residential planning clearance before the permit is issued.
Follow the review in the portal's Application Progress tab, where Mesa County and review agencies upload comments that may need your attention.

Schedule inspections on the Customer Portal, by phone at 970-256-1564, or by texting SCHEDULE to 844-987-4628. Requests received by 7:00 a.m. can be scheduled for the same day or the next business day.
When an inspection is complete, see the results and inspector comments by clicking on the inspection in the portal.
If Xcel Energy is your utility, Xcel works with you and your contractors to witness test and energize the system, and the process ends with a permission to operate letter from Xcel.
inspection_steps.notes: The County's inspection page does not say which inspections apply to a solar permit. It links the Building Sample Inspection Codes 02-05-24 and the Residential Inspection Guidelines; ask the Building Department which inspections apply when you schedule. The County permit, the County inspections and the utility's permission to operate are separate approvals.

timeline_days.notes: The County's Building Department pages give no review time for a solar permit.

value.program_or_pathway: Mesa County Building Department permit for a PV system, applied for on the Customer Portal
other_conditions: A rapid shutdown function to reduce shock hazard for firefighters is required.
DC circuits in buildings require metal raceways and labeling of "PHOTOVOLTAIC POWER SOURCE".
Roof mount systems require a residential planning clearance before issuance if the system is in De Beque, Collbran, or Palisade.
Commercial systems in the city limits of Grand Junction and in unincorporated Mesa County require a planning and fire clearance.

The PV guide says design criteria shall include wind speed (115 mph) and snow loads by elevation from the Adopted Codes and Regulations page. That page lists a basic wind speed (residential only) of 104 for Grand Junction and surrounding area and does not name Clifton, so confirm the design wind speed and snow load for your site with the Building Department.

The PV guide lists the 2018 IBC, IRC, IEBC, IFC and the 2023 NEC, while the County's Adopted Codes and Regulations page lists the 2024 International Residential Code. Confirm the code edition with the Building Department.
The County says the 2026 NEC will be effective January 1, 2027.

Xcel Energy interconnection limits (not a County rule): expected generation, combined with other generation at the address, must not exceed 200% of the previous 12 months of use, and all equipment must be UL 1741 SB certified and on the California Energy Commission Solar Equipment Lists.

permit_fees.notes: Mesa County's fee schedule has no separate solar line: the permit fee follows the valuation table (Table 2) in Exhibit A, the Mesa County Building Department Fee Schedule (file titled Fee Schedule 2024). For remodel work and other building upgrades, the County bases the fee on the valuation of the project, and the schedule defines total valuation as the actual cost of project labor and materials. The schedule lists the electrical permit fee (fee 11) on the same Table 2 basis. The PV guide asks for a valuation that includes all labor and materials. All permit fees are rounded up to the next dollar, and the table continues above $50,000. Other fees may be assessed depending on the scope of the project. Exhibit A also lists a residential submittal fee (maximum of $250, non-refundable, applied to the permit fee at the time of issuance) for residential projects that hold a risk of non-issuance after staff intake and review, as determined by the Building Official, $100.00 for an additional re-inspection on the same violation, and twice the permit fee for work started before the permit is issued, at the Building Official's discretion.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Income Qualified upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says customers who qualify under the terms of Income Qualified can receive an upfront rebate of $3 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer and qualify under Xcel's Income Qualified terms. Check that Xcel Energy is your utility first.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Disproportionately Impacted Communities upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says Disproportionately Impacted Communities can receive an upfront rebate of $0.50 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer. Check that Xcel Energy is your utility first.

rebates.notes: Xcel's page says that as of 10/05/2026 it moved $1,050,000 from Solar*Rewards C&I to the Solar*Rewards Residential IQ/DIC program. The County's pages describe no County rebate for residential solar.
